subject: Term sync & pricing tier addendum — final redlines and signature path
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@cygnushealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Term sync & pricing tier addendum — final redlines and signature path

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I’m sending the consolidated package so your contracts team can redline the Order Form and Exhibit B with the agreed uplift and the 24-month term. Key points we discussed:

- Extend base term from 12 months to 24 months with a mid-term review after month 12.
- Add a usage-based uplifts schedule (see Exhibit B, lines 3–6) to capture the anticipated quarterly spikes.
- SLA: keep standard SLA but add a 30-day credit cap for the first renewal year.

Attached: Redwood_OrderForm_v4_Cygnus.pdf — this includes the exhibit updates we talked through. Once you return redlines, I’ll loop in Legal (Marissa) for a quick pass.

Next steps: could you have your contracts team send back a redline PDF or Word by Friday? If there are any material changes to scope/usage we should surface them now so we can quantify delta on pricing.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

---
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@cygnushealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@cygnushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Term sync & pricing tier addendum — final redlines and signature path

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for sending. Attached is our working redline (Cygnus_Redlines_v3.docx). High-level notes from our side:

- Term: we are ok with 24 months but request an option to terminate after 12 months for cause with 60 days’ notice tied to data residency commitments.
- Pricing: we accepted the uplift bands but asked for a clearer definition of "burst" in Exhibit B (proposed wording in the doc).
- Data retention: added a request to clarify log retention for debugging (30 days vs 90 days).
- Procurement needs a single line item for the Dedicated pool charge for invoicing simplification.

We’ve highlighted proposed language. Please confirm you’ve received the file and whether Redwood Legal is comfortable with the proposed termination clause.

Olivia
Olivia Chen
Head of IT Ops, Cygnus Health
olivia.chen@cygnushealth.com
[Attachment: Cygnus_Redlines_v3.docx (docx)]

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: vanessa@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, olivia.chen@cygnushealth.com, contracts@cygnushealth.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Term sync & pricing tier addendum — final redlines and signature path

Vanessa —

Thanks for the ping and Olivia — thanks for the redlines. I reviewed Cygnus_Redlines_v3.docx and flagged two items for discussion:

1) Termination after 12 months for cause tied to data residency — we can agree to a for-cause termination right, but need to narrow the trigger language (suggest: "material failure to comply with agreed data residency terms after 30 days’ written notice and failure to cure"). The current language is broader than we can accept.

2) Burst definition — we can add a concrete metric: define a burst as any 1-hour period where sustained throughput exceeds 3x the monthly median rate for that tenant, limited to X occurrences per billing quarter (we'll propose 4). Ops and Dedicated engineering will need to confirm the 3x/4 occurrences number; tagging karthik for a quick sanity check.

I’ve made inline suggestions in the attached mark-up and created a slim redline we can send back to Contracts. If Cygnus wants a Dedicated pool line item, Finance will need the exact SKU for invoicing — Vanessa, can you confirm the SKU and monthly commitment amount?

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

[Attachment: Redwood_OrderForm_Markup_v1.pdf (pdf)]

---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vanessa@redwood.com
Cc: olivia.chen@cygnushealth.com, contracts@cygnushealth.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Term sync & pricing tier addendum — final redlines and signature path

Marissa / Vanessa —

Quick Ops confirmation on the burst metric: 3x monthly median is reasonable as a proxy, but I recommend we use a more conservative operational threshold for the first renewal year: 2.5x and cap to 3 incidents per billing quarter (so we have predictability). Also: define "sustained" as a 15-minute rolling window rather than 1 hour to align with our telemetry.

SKU for Dedicated pool (provisional): DED-16-GPU-MPK (monthly commitment $52,000) — finance to confirm final billing code.

If Cygnus accepts 2.5x / 3 incidents / 15-minute window, signal and Marissa will fold it into the redline.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure Ops | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

---
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@cygnushealth.com>
To: vanessa@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@cygnushealth.com
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 16:44:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Term sync & pricing tier addendum — final redlines and signature path

Thanks all —

Cygnus is comfortable with the revised operational thresholds: 2.5x, 3 incidents per quarter, 15-minute sustained window. We’ve removed the unconditional 12-month termination and replaced it with the narrower for-cause language Marissa proposed. Contracts asked that the Dedicated pool SKU appear as a separate invoice line; that’s acceptable.

Next: can Redwood send back a slim redline PDF reflecting the 2.5x / 3 incidents / 15-minute language and the invoice line item? Procurement would like the final doc by Tuesday EOD to allow AP to set up the purchase order. If everything is green, we’ll route via DocuSign.

Olivia
Olivia Chen
Head of IT Ops, Cygnus Health
